item.title: In 1970s, Marty Bluewater bought land on island planned for 800 homes; he is now its only resident
item.description: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.

item.title: US Air Force major held again days after arrest for calling for Trump’s impeachment
item.description: A US Air Force major, Jason Watson, finds himself detained once more for voicing his criticism of President Trump and advocating for his impeachment. Currently in pretrial confinement, Watson's refusal to wear his military uniform led to this latest arrest. This incident follows his earlier detention on the Capitol steps for expressing political opinions, showcasing his awareness of the repercussions he faces for his stance.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Oldest evidence of life on Earth has been discovered in India in a 3.4 billion-year-old layered rock shows signs of microbial life
item.description: Recent discoveries in India have unveiled biological traces that date back approximately 3.5 billion years, indicating a significantly ancient origin of life on Earth. Researchers have confirmed the presence of photosynthetic activity and intricate metabolic processes within these samples, which originated from environments close to underwater hydrothermal vents. This remarkable finding represents the oldest known biological materials found in rock formations.

item.title: Scientists simulate nuclear strike to stop a 160-metre asteroid impact
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, scientists conducted simulations showcasing the potential of nuclear warheads to neutralize hazardous asteroids. These experiments focused on strategies for fragmenting large asteroids prior to their collision with Earth. While this approach holds promise for planetary protection, it is viewed as a last resort, especially for threats detected late. Ongoing research is crucial for insights into fragment dynamics and their long-lasting consequences.

item.title: Pulitzer Prize-winning poet bought a barren land in Hawaii and turned it into a 19-acre forest with more than 3,000 palms
item.description: W.S. Merwin, a celebrated poet, found solace and seclusion in Maui during the 1970s, where he dedicated himself to creating a lush 19-acre palm forest. This extraordinary project transformed a barren piece of land into a thriving ecological haven, showcasing an impressive array of palm species. Today, the Merwin Conservancy diligently safeguards this rich environmental legacy, ensuring it remains a vital part of our natural heritage.

item.title: Missouri engineer hand-built an underground home into a hillside; 50yrs later, it remains leak-free
item.description: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Giant 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire after nearly 90 years as scientists explain UK return
item.description: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1963, a California builder made a house that rotates 320 degrees using two washing-machine motors
item.description: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Maine’s Millinocket lost more than jobs after 2008 mill closure; locals now hope for revival
item.description: Millinocket, Maine, once thrived around Great Northern Paper Company, but the mill’s 2008 closure transformed the community. In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.

item.title: Valkyrae Defends Thumbnail Artist: streamer says Uncharted art is not AI; warns on artists’ jobs
item.description: Valkyrae has addressed AI allegations surrounding her YouTube thumbnails after viewers accused her latest Uncharted artwork of being AI-generated. She defended her longtime artist, Anko, explaining that he creates her livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his creative process. Valkyrae said she understands why people may suspect AI but stressed, “But it’s not AI.” She also expressed concern about AI threatening artists’ jobs and livelihoods.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Owens Questions SD Card Handling: Video shows Terrell pocket card; chain of custody remains debated
item.description: Candace Owens’ newly highlighted footage has reignited scrutiny over an SD card removed from a camera positioned behind Charlie Kirk. Owens questions why the card was allegedly taken so quickly and why the person involved appeared to use his phone rather than collect other cards. She stresses that her interpretation is opinion, while raising questions about the footage’s handling, possible communication and why that recording was prioritized.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Viral Ice Poseidon Poster Debunked: Checks show image is citizen-made; police have issued no warrant
item.description: Ice Poseidon’s latest Japan controversy has raised fresh questions after a “wanted poster” appeared online. The streamer has faced police questioning, business restrictions and public backlash during previous trips. His recent return to Japan has also brought another confrontation involving a Pokémon store.
